lines.text: House Corrow had one answer for everything on the Senn. A great iron chain, from bank to bank. For trade, for war, and apparently for me.
A Corrow boat rowed out to meet us. Lady Sabine stood in the bow in violet furs, fanning herself in the cold out of pure habit.
Corvin. You look employed.
My lady. You look exactly the same. I mean that as a warning.
Lucan Varr. Hollow-born, traitor, and worth ten thousand crowns. Do you know what that buys? Three warships. Or one very grateful Grand Measurer.
Her men had crossbows. We had a wounded knight, a drained Measurer, an archer with four arrows, a clerk, a spy, a child and me. I did the maths.
I can get four of them.
Not yet, Wren. So, my lady. Why haven't you sold me already?
Because warships sink, and grateful men forget. I've been sold to Vance myself, Lord Lucan. I know exactly what he pays.
She touched the ring on her finger, very lightly, the way you touch a bruise. Then she looked downriver, toward Aldcrown.
The morning after your fire, the Grand Measurer invited my son and daughter to stay at the Order's College. As his guests. For as long as he likes.
It was the only time I ever heard Lady Sabine's voice shake.
So. I lift my chain, and I never saw you. In return, you owe me a favour. One. Of my choosing, when I choose.
Not a life. Not a bond. And not Saltmouth.
Oh, nothing so dull. I'll know it when I need it. So will you.
Lucan. A favour to Sabine Corrow is a knife you hand her, handle first.
I know. One favour, my lady. Done.
We shook hands across the water. Her glove was cold. My hand was colder. She noticed.
I told you once I wouldn't make the same mistake twice. I'm not. This time, I'm betting on you.
The great chain sank into the river with a sound like a bell under water, and our barge slid over it.
She'll collect, my lord. She always collects. I kept the ledger.
Two days upriver, the banners on the bank changed from violet to black and gold. My father's colours.
The last time I'd seen him, he had begged me to run. I hadn't run. I didn't know what he would say.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and thirteen, coming soon.
